title: Setting Up Your Development Environment
description: Install the .NET 8.0 SDK, set up Visual Studio 2022 or VS Code, and verify your environment is ready for ASP.NET Core MVC development.

data.text: Before you write any ASP.NET Core code, you need a working development environment. This lesson walks you through installing the **.NET 8.0 SDK**, choosing an editor, and confirming everything works with a single terminal command.
What Is the .NET SDK?

The **.NET Software Development Kit (SDK)** is everything you need to build and run .NET applications. It includes the C# compiler (`csc`), the `dotnet` command-line tool, runtime libraries, and templates for scaffolding new projects. Without the SDK, your machine cannot understand or execute C# code.

data.title: Runtime vs SDK
data.text: The .NET Runtime lets you run existing apps. The .NET SDK lets you build them. Always install the SDK — the runtime is installed automatically alongside it.
Choose an Editor
ASP.NET Core MVC works with any text editor, but two tools dominate the ecosystem.

data.title: Visual Studio 2022 vs Visual Studio Code

cards.title: Visual Studio 2022
cards.description: Microsoft's full-featured IDE for Windows and macOS.
pros: Integrated debugger, profiler, and database tools
Built-in project templates and scaffolding wizards
Seamless Azure and IIS deployment integration
cons: Professional edition requires a paid license

cards.title: Visual Studio Code
cards.description: Lightweight, cross-platform, open-source editor from Microsoft.
pros: Free and runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux
Fast startup and low resource footprint
C# Dev Kit extension provides full IntelliSense and debugging
Terminal-first workflow great for CLI and Git users
cons: Requires manual extension installation for C# support
No built-in visual designers for WinForms or WPF

data.text: For this course you can use either tool. The code examples are identical regardless of editor. If you are on Linux or prefer a fast editor, choose VS Code. If you want the most guided experience on Windows, choose Visual Studio 2022 Community.
Install the .NET 8.0 SDK

The official download page always lists the latest supported SDK versions. Navigate to [dotnet.microsoft.com/download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download) and download the **.NET 8.0 SDK** (not just the runtime) for your operating system.

data.title: Verify the Version
data.text: This course targets .NET 8.0. Run `dotnet --version` after installation and confirm it prints `8.0.xxx`. If it prints a 6.0 or 7.0 version, download and install the 8.0 SDK separately.

data.title: Windows Installation Steps
items: Download the `.exe` installer (x64 or Arm64 depending on your machine).
Run the installer and follow the on-screen prompts.
Open a new PowerShell or Command Prompt window — the `dotnet` command must run in a fresh terminal.
Run `dotnet --list-sdks` and confirm `8.0.xxx` appears in the output.

data.title: macOS Installation Steps
items: Download the `.pkg` installer from the download page.
Open the package and complete the installation wizard.
Open a new Terminal window.
Run `dotnet --list-sdks` to confirm the 8.0 SDK is listed.

data.title: Linux Installation Steps
items: Add the Microsoft package repository for your distribution.
Install with your package manager, e.g. `sudo apt install dotnet-sdk-8.0` on Ubuntu/Debian.
Run `dotnet --list-sdks` to verify.

data.text: Set Up Visual Studio Code

VS Code does not include C# support by default. After installing VS Code, install the **C# Dev Kit** extension published by Microsoft. It bundles IntelliSense, debugging, project management, and test explorers in one package.

data.title: VS Code Setup Checklist
items: Install VS Code from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com).
Open VS Code and go to the Extensions view (`Ctrl+Shift+X` / `Cmd+Shift+X`).
Search for **C# Dev Kit** and install it.
Restart VS Code when prompted.
Open the Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P` / `Cmd+Shift+P`) and run **.NET: New Project** to confirm the extension is active.

data.title: Command Palette Shortcuts
data.text: The .NET Dev Kit adds many commands to the Command Palette. Try typing `.NET:` to see all available commands — New Project, Build, Debug, Test, and more.
Create Your First Project with the CLI
The `dotnet` CLI is the fastest way to scaffold and run projects. You do not need Visual Studio at all — everything below works identically in PowerShell, Terminal, or Command Prompt.

terms.definition: The cross-platform command-line toolchain for .NET. Commands include `dotnet new`, `dotnet build`, `dotnet run`, and `dotnet test`.
A pre-built project skeleton included with the SDK. `mvc` is the template for ASP.NET Core MVC apps.
A container that groups one or more projects. Visual Studio uses it; the CLI works fine without it for single-project apps.

data.caption: How the dotnet CLI turns a template into a running web app.
data.definition:
flowchart LR A["dotnet new mvc -n MyApp"] --> B["Creates project folder
+ Program.cs + _Layout.cshtml"] B --> C["dotnet run"] C --> D["Kestrel starts on http://localhost:5000"] D --> E["Browser shows the app"]

data.title: Create and Run an MVC Project
items: Open a terminal and navigate to the folder where you want to store your projects.
Run: `dotnet new mvc -n FirstApp` — this creates a folder called `FirstApp` with a complete MVC project.
Run: `cd FirstApp` to enter the project folder.
Run: `dotnet run` — the CLI builds and launches the app using the built-in Kestrel web server.
Look for the line `Now listening on: http://localhost:5000` in the terminal output.
Open a browser and navigate to `http://localhost:5000` to see the default home page.

data.title: Terminal Session
data.content: Creating and running your first ASP.NET Core MVC app from the command line.
data.code:
# Create a new MVC project
> dotnet new mvc -n FirstApp

# Enter the project folder
> cd FirstApp

# Build and run the app
> dotnet run
Building...
Build succeeded in 2.3s
Now listening on: http://localhost:5000
Application started. Press Ctrl+C to shut down.

data.text: Verify Your Installation
Run the following command to confirm the SDK, runtime, and templates are all installed correctly:

data.title: Verification Commands
data.content: Run each command to verify a part of your .NET installation.
data.code:
dotnet --version
# Expected: 8.0.xxx

dotnet --list-sdks
# Should show 8.0.xxx listed

dotnet --list-runtimes
# Should show Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 8.0.xxx

dotnet new --list
# Should show 'mvc' template in the list

data.title: Stuck on an Old Version?
data.text: If `dotnet --version` returns a number lower than 8.0, the older SDK is running from a folder earlier in your system PATH. Uninstall older versions from "Add or Remove Programs" (Windows) or `/usr/local/share/dotnet` (macOS/Linux), then restart your terminal.
What Is Kestrel?

When you run `dotnet run`, ASP.NET Core uses a built-in, cross-platform web server called **Kestrel**. Kestrel is fast and production-capable. In production you may place it behind a reverse proxy like Nginx or IIS, but during development Kestrel is all you need — no extra setup required.

data.caption: Kestrel handles HTTP requests directly during development.

http://localhost:5000"] -->|HTTP Request| Kestrel["Kestrel Web Server
(built into dotnet run)"]
    Kestrel -->|Invokes| App["ASP.NET Core MVC App
(Program.cs)"]

data.text: Stop and Restart the App

Every time you change C# code you must rebuild and restart the app. Use `Ctrl+C` in the terminal to stop it, then `dotnet run` again. Hot reload is available in .NET 6+ — the CLI will tell you when it has applied changes without a full restart.

data.title: Exercise: Verify Your Environment
data.description: Complete every step below and check each item off when you are done.
steps: Install the .NET 8.0 SDK from the official download page.
Open a new terminal and run `dotnet --version`. Confirm it returns `8.0.xxx`.
Run `dotnet new --list` and confirm `mvc` appears in the output.
Run `dotnet new mvc -n FirstApp` to scaffold a new project.
Open `http://localhost:5000` in your browser and confirm the default ASP.NET Core home page loads.
data.expectedOutcome: A working ASP.NET Core MVC app running locally with no errors in the terminal.

items.text: Chosen and installed an editor (Visual Studio 2022 or VS Code)
items.hint: VS Code users: also install the C# Dev Kit extension.

items.text: First project created with `dotnet new mvc`
items.hint: The `FirstApp` folder should contain Program.cs, a Controllers folder, and a Views folder.
You should see the default ASP.NET Core welcome page in the browser.

items.question: Do I need Visual Studio to build ASP.NET Core MVC apps?
items.answer: No. The `dotnet` CLI can create, build, and run any ASP.NET Core project. Visual Studio is a convenience IDE, not a requirement.

items.question: Can I use .NET 9.0 or .NET 10.0 instead?
items.answer: This course targets .NET 8.0. Newer SDKs can usually build older target frameworks, but for the smoothest experience install the .NET 8.0 SDK specifically.

items.question: What is the difference between the SDK and the runtime?
items.answer: The SDK contains compilers and build tools — you need it to write code. The runtime executes compiled apps — end users need only the runtime.

items.question: Why does the app listen on port 5000 by default?
items.answer: Kestrel's default HTTP binding is `http://localhost:5000` and HTTPS is `https://localhost:5001`. These can be changed in `Program.cs` or via the `ASPNETCORE_URLS` environment variable.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The .NET 8.0 SDK includes the compiler, CLI tools, and project templates needed to build ASP.NET Core apps.
Visual Studio 2022 is a full IDE for Windows; VS Code is a lightweight cross-platform editor — both work equally well.
`dotnet new mvc -n FirstApp` scaffolds a complete MVC project in seconds.
`dotnet run` builds and launches Kestrel, the built-in development web server.
Always open a fresh terminal after installing the SDK so the `dotnet` command is available.
data.takeaway: With your environment verified, you are ready to understand what ASP.NET Core MVC actually is and how it is structured.
